content: If you miss a dose of your medication, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication in its original container at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in July 2024. It is important to note that this document provides a summary and does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Before taking this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, tenofovir, or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. This medication may cause dizziness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you are sure you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. This medication is not recommended for use during pregnancy, as it may not work effectively in pregnant women. If you become pregnant or suspect you may be pregnant, inform your doctor immediately. Emtricitabine and tenofovir are known to pass into breast milk, but it is unclear if elvitegravir or cobicistat do so. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor if you are breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Do not take this medication with other HIV medications, such as ritonavir. This medication may slow the removal of other drugs from your body, potentially affecting their efficacy. Similarly, other medications may influence the removal of this drug from your body, altering its effectiveness. Examples include mitotane and rifampin. This medication may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods, such as pills, patches, or rings, potentially leading to pregnancy. It may also increase the risk of certain side effects associated with hormonal birth control. Discuss alternative reliable forms of birth control with your doctor, and use an effective barrier method (e.g., latex or polyurethane condoms, dental dams) during sexual activity to reduce the risk of spreading HIV to others. In the event of an overdose, if the individual has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Laboratory and medical tests (e.g., kidney and liver function, hepatitis B virus testing, viral load, T-cell counts, blood mineral levels, bone density tests, urine glucose/protein levels) should be conducted before starting this medication and periodically while taking it.
